title: Introduce shadow trace replay engine for low-overhead tail analysis
creator: Asha Patel
description: Problem: tail-latency and error debugging today requires full trace capture which adds measurable overhead to hotpaths (allocations, extra headers, span encoding). Goal: reduce production tracing perturbation by capturing a tiny, monotonic event log on the hotpath and reconstructing full traces off-path via a replay service ("shadow trace replayer") when we detect anomalies. This keeps the hotpath cheap while preserving the ability to inspect complete trace graphs for post-hoc analysis of errors and latency outliers.
background: We have attempted several hotpath sampling optimizations (adaptive prefilters, early exits, probabilistic samplers) but still see cases where either too many traces are dropped or the overhead of span assembly remains non-negligible for high-qps endpoints. Shadow replay separates capture from assembly: emit compact event tokens (fingerprint + timestamp + small tag set) synchronously; stream events to a durable log; when an outlier is flagged (metrics, error spike, or manual request), the replayer pulls related logs, application request logs, and metric timelines to reconstruct the trace offline.
acceptance_criteria: Hotpath overhead: synchronous impact on p50/p95 latency for instrumented endpoints must be <= 0.5% compared to no-tracing baseline
Event size: per-request synchronous footprint (token + metadata) must be <= 64 bytes on average
Replayer can reconstruct 90% of spans for replayed requests using logs + stored KV snapshots in test environment
Console: given a request-id or anomaly window, UI can surface a reconstructed trace within 30s for 95% of cases
Fallback: if the replayer cannot fully reconstruct a trace, it surfaces partial span graph and provenance of missing pieces
implementation_notes: Ingress proxy / SDK changes: embed 16-byte request fingerprint + 1-byte sampling flag + optional 1-2 small tag bytes; emit lightweight event to telemetry pipeline synchronously (non-blocking write to fast buffer)
Streaming: use existing Kafka topic 'trace-events-compact' with compressed batches; design schema to be forward-compatible and cheap to encode
Cold store: retain compact event shards for 72 hours in S3 with index by fingerprint and time range; keep pointer to logs and metric windows

Replayer service: on-demand job that gathers events + raw logs + request-level KV snapshots (where available) and runs assembly heuristics to materialize spans; run in dedicated worker pool to avoid impacting serving clusters
UI integration: add 'Reconstruct trace' action on the latency/error dashboard that kicks a replayer job and streams progress to user; show provenance metadata when reconstruction is partial

Instrumentation fallback: when full tracing is enabled for a tenant, the system should still support full-span emission path; shadow replay must not change sampling semantics for tenants that opted into full tracing
Data protection: event payloads must not contain PII; use config-driven scrubbing and integrate with KMS for encryption at-rest for S3 shards
rollout_plan: A: Spike - implement prototype for single internal service (payments-svc) with shadow events written to dev Kafka and replayer running against dev logs (done)
B: Canary - enable in staging for two customer-like workloads and validate hotpath latency/allocations over 48h
C: Gradual - enable for 10% of production traffic on low-latency tier; monitor error budget, tail-latency, and downstream storage costs
D: Full - flip default to 'shadow-enabled' for new tenants, provide config to opt-out, and document SLA/retention trade-offs
E: Observe - maintain dashboard: 'shadow replay success rate', 'avg reconstruct time', 'hotpath latency delta' and run 1-week post-rollout review
risks: Underestimated storage cost for shards and replayer replays—need accurate retention cost model
Incomplete reconstruction if app logs or KV snapshots are unavailable—will need graceful UI messaging
Potential privacy exposure if event schema accidentally carries sensitive keys—strict schema review required
Operational complexity: replayer jobs may load S3/log stores heavily when multiple users request reconstructions concurrently
